LESSON: USES OF BODY PARTS • MOUTH • EYES • LEGS • HANDS • EARS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Myself
Topic 1.2: Uses of Body Parts • Mouth • Eyes • Legs • Hands • Ears
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Uses of Body Parts • Mouth • Eyes • Legs • Hands • Ears, part of Myself in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: How do we use parts of our body?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Uses of Body Parts • Mouth • Eyes • Legs • Hands • Ears together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self- efficacy: learner know more about self when role playing the uses of body parts

Values:
• Love: learner develops love when sharing playing materials.

• Peace: learner cares and respects self and others when singing songs on uses of body parts.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Developmental perspectives: learner develops self - awareness when naming external body parts.

Link to other learning area:

Uses of body parts relates to concepts of attentive listening to stories in Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

A theme-based multi-purpose communication board/ chart/ picture cut-outs/ name cards on uses of external body parts, adapted

cutting tools such as scissors with padded handles, padded pencils and crayons with grips, positioning/ seating devices whose

worktops/ table tops are at a suitable height, adhesive such as masking tape, slant boards, mobility devices, typing aid, head

mouse, universal cuffs, adapted digital device with special accessibility features and software, universal cuffs and pens/ sticks,

pictures depicting people performing various actions and which body parts are in use, special seating devices with adjustable

height

Other Related Service Providers: Physiotherapist, Learner support Assistant/ Scribe
